title: Serialization Tax in Shared-Latent Exchangeable Decisions
abstract: arXiv:2611.26029v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Accurate item probabilities can produce inaccurate group-level decisions. A system may score each item separately, yet act on whether enough hidden items succeed: show a slate, defer a panel decision, or inspect a batch. When items share an uncertain latent state, independent marginalization preserves means but removes dependence from the aggregate posterior. We call this error the serialization tax. For binary items sharing one success rate, classical convex-order comparisons give a more dispersed exact count law than any independent completion with the same total mean. We quantify variance and total-variation gaps, derive threshold separation under margin conditions, and connect posterior approximation to decision regret. Separate results cover non-binary outcomes, heterogeneous items, and sufficient posterior resolution. TaxScore identifies large hidden blocks with unresolved uncertainty near a decision boundary for routing to richer

translated_title: 共享潜在状态可交换决策中的串行化税
translated_abstract: 准确的单项概率也可能产生不准确的群体层面决策。一个系统可能对每个条目分别评分，但其行动却取决于是否有足够多的隐藏条目成功：例如展示一版推荐列表、推迟一个小组决策，或检查一整批样本。当各条目共享一个不确定的潜在状态时，独立的边缘化虽然能保持均值，却会从聚合后验中移除相关性。我们将这种误差称为“串行化税”。对于共享同一成功率的二元条目，经典的凸序比较表明，精确计数的分布比任何具有相同总均值的独立补全模型都更为分散。我们量化了方差差距与全变差差距，在边际条件下推导了阈值分离，并将后验近似与决策遗憾联系起来。其他独立的结果涵盖了非二元结果、异质条目以及充分后验分辨率的情形。TaxScore 能够识别处于决策边界附近且不确定性未消除的大型隐藏块，以便将其路由至更丰富的（推断流程）。
tldr: 本文提出“串行化税”概念：当条目共享不确定的潜在状态时，独立边缘化虽保持均值却破坏了聚合后验中的相关性，作者用凸序比较量化方差与全变差差距、推导阈值分离并连接决策遗憾，进而提出 TaxScore 识别决策边界附近存在未消解不确定性的大型隐藏块以引导更强的推断。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the "serialization tax"—the error where independently marginalizing items that share an uncertain latent state preserves means but destroys dependence in the aggregate posterior—quantifies it via convex-order comparisons (variance and total-variation gaps, threshold separation under margin conditions), links posterior approximation to decision regret, and proposes TaxScore to flag large hidden blocks with unresolved uncertainty near decision boundaries for routing to richer inference.
